For treatment of type 2 diabetes in children and adolescents, lifestyle management, also taught through DSMES, is foundational, and pharmacologic treatment with or without insulin is necessary.

Evidence suggests that type 2 diabetes in children and adolescents is different not only from type 1 diabetes but also from type 2 diabetes in adults and has unique features, such as a more rapidly progressive decline in β-cell function and accelerated development of diabetes complications.
